scenario.prompt_to_agent:
All Campus 1 PCs (PC5-14) report Campus 2 (10.5.0.x, 10.6.0.x)
is unreachable. Intra-Campus-1 traffic still works. Campus 2
hosts can still reach each other internally. Find the failure
between the campuses.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: mswitch0 ospfd
Mechanism: mswitch0 is Campus 1's multilayer switch — it owns
  the L3 gateways for VLAN 10/20/30 (172.16.10/20/30.254)
  and runs OSPF to advertise these subnets into the backbone.
  Without ospfd, Campus 1 prefixes age out of router16, router7,
  and onward. Campus 2 still has routes intact (their
  advertiser sshswitch/router17 is unaffected) but Campus 1
  becomes invisible.
Localization: mswitch0
Root cause: ospfd not running on mswitch0
Fix: restart FRR AND re-apply the `router ospf` configuration on mswitch0 (see [FIX] -- a bare restart alone does not restore the vtysh-applied config).

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on mswitch0" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`/etc/init.d/frr restart` on mswitch0

NOTE (lab-verified 2026-07-03): this lab applies FRR config via vtysh at boot (there is no /etc/frr/frr.conf), so `/etc/init.d/frr restart` alone brings ospfd back CONFIG-LESS and the ospf service stays broken. The complete remediation is to (re)start FRR/ospfd AND re-apply the `router ospf` configuration (network statements) on mswitch0. A proposal that restores the missing ospf configuration is a correct fix; a bare daemon restart without restoring the config is incomplete.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is the failure of the OSPF daemon (ospfd) on mswitch0, the
Campus 1 multilayer switch. mswitch0 acts as the Layer-3 default gateway
for all Campus 1 PCs (PC5–PC14) via three VLAN SVIs: 172.16.10.254
(VLAN 10), 172.16.20.254 (VLAN 20), and 172.16.30.254 (VLAN 30). Its
startup script enables ospfd and attempts to join OSPF area 0 by
advertising the four directly-connected prefixes (10.2.2.0/24,
172.16.10.0/24, 172.16.20.0/24, 172.16.30.0/24) via vtysh. However,
ospfd failed at startup and is not running ("Status of ospfd: FAILED").
/etc/frr/ospfd.conf is present but empty (0 bytes), so no OSPF
configuration was persisted; ospfd has nothing to load on start and
crashes or refuses to initialize.

As a direct consequence, mswitch0's routing table holds only four
directly-connected prefixes and has no route toward Campus 2 (10.5.0.0/24,
10.6.0.0/24). When a Campus 1 PC sends a packet to a Campus 2 address,
it is forwarded to its default gateway on mswitch0, which black-holes it
(no matching route, no default route). Intra-Campus-1 traffic is unaffected
because those destinations (172.16.10/20/30.0/24) are directly connected
on mswitch0. Campus 2 internal traffic is also unaffected because it never
transits mswitch0. The rest of the OSPF fabric (router16, router7, router10,
router8, router17) is healthy and has full inter-campus routing.

Root cause: ospfd is not running on mswitch0 because ospfd.conf is empty,
leaving the Campus 1 multilayer switch with no OSPF routes and no path to
Campus 2.

Corrective fix: Populate /etc/frr/ospfd.conf with the required OSPF
configuration (router ospf, network 10.2.2.0/24 area 0, network
172.16.10.0/24 area 0, network 172.16.20.0/24 area 0, network
172.16.30.0/24 area 0), then restart FRR on mswitch0
(/etc/init.d/frr restart). ospfd will come up, form an OSPF adjacency
with router16 over the 10.2.2.0/24 link, and install inter-campus routes.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies mswitch0 as the affected device and centers the diagnosis on its ospfd failure.
The submission explicitly identifies the OSPF daemon (ospfd) on mswitch0 as the failed component and attributes the outage to ospfd/OSPF being nonfunctional.
The writeup proposes restoring the missing OSPF configuration in /etc/frr/ospfd.conf (router ospf + network statements) and restarting FRR, which matches the expected remediation.

The agent's log contains direct observations that ospfd is down on mswitch0, mswitch0 has only connected routes, and PCs point to mswitch0 as gateway; the writeup's inferences (missing/empty OSPF config leading to ospfd failure and loss of inter-campus routes) follow logically and the proposed fix matches the observed misconfiguration. Minor ambiguity about a few file contents (truncated outputs) prevents a perfect score.
